enervate

EN-ur-vayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To enervate is to weaken or drain energy from someone.

The thick, humid air seemed to enervate everyone on the crowded platform.

Example

Weeks of poor sleep had gradually enervated the entire night shift.

This wasn't ordinary tiredness -- it was a steady draining of strength and vitality over time, which is exactly enervate.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

weaken: To weaken is the all-purpose word for lowering strength of any kind, for any reason, at any speed. To enervate is narrower: it drains a person's energy and vitality specifically, and it does its work gradually — humid air, poor sleep, long strain wearing someone down.

sap: To sap strength is to bleed it away slowly, a little at a time, often before anyone notices the loss. Enervate is its close formal cousin, and the shared core is gradualness: both words describe a long, quiet draining rather than one sudden effort.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

invigorate: give strength and energy to

Where it sits · how completely the strength is drained

tire → enervate → exhaust

tire vs. enervate: Getting tired is an ordinary, temporary state; enervating drains someone's strength more deeply and over a longer time.

exhaust vs. enervate: Enervate describes a gradual draining of energy; exhaust implies the strength has already run out completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — e-: out (Latin (ex-))

root — nerv: sinew, nerve (Latin (nervus))

suffix — -ate: to make or perform an action (Latin)

Put it together: Enervate comes from Latin e- ('out') + nervus ('sinew, nerve') + -ate -- literally 'to remove the sinew from,' leaving something without its strength.

Use the root in a new word: nerve: The same nervus root gives us the everyday word nerve, both for the body's nerve fibers and, non-literally, for courage or boldness.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Enervate is a classic false friend for "energize" -- despite sounding similar, enervate means the exact opposite, draining energy rather than adding it.
